---
title: "How do I import a CSV and confirm the fields were read correctly?"
---

## The question

How do I import a CSV and confirm the fields were read correctly?

## What to check and do

1. Locate an actual CSV. 2. Use read.csv() to load it as a data frame. 3. Inspect names, types, rows and missing values before calculating anything.

## Worked example: iris

This example uses a public dataset distributed with R. It does not make claims about observations outside that dataset.

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("iris")
csv <- tempfile(fileext=".csv")
write.csv(d, csv, row.names=FALSE)
imported <- ru_apply("import_csv", file=csv)
stopifnot(nrow(imported)==150L, identical(names(imported),names(d)))
unlink(csv)
```

The round-trip import retains the Iris flower measurements and species names. For an actual CSV, pass its real path instead of creating a temporary file.

## Apply the method to another question

Replace the data frame and column names with those in your own file:

```r
ru_apply("import_csv", file="path/to/measurements.csv")
```

Questions about a broken file path require checking the working directory and file name before using any statistical function.


## Inspect conditions

Use `ru_plan("import_csv")` for available-versus-missing input routes. A calculation can run even when its assumptions do not justify an inference.
